biography.plain_text: Theodoros Vassilakis was a Greek businessman who built Autohellas and founded Aegean Airlines. Born in Heraklion, Crete, he entered car rental with his wife, Emmanouela, before acquiring Hertz's Greek business and expanding into vehicle dealerships. His later airline venture grew from domestic services into an international carrier and acquired Olympic Air.

long_biography.plain_text:
Greek entrepreneur Theodoros Vassilakis promoted golf as a way to attract visitors beyond the summer holiday season. He helped develop the Crete Golf Club and argued for courses near Athens, linked with holiday homes and other tourism facilities. Regulatory questions, he cautioned, needed resolving before those investments could proceed.

He chaired the organising committee of the Aegean Airlines Pro-Am. Its 2013 tournament at Costa Navarino paired one professional with three amateurs in each team. Alongside the competition, football internationals and golf professionals ran joint coaching sessions, with younger players taking part. The event also used electronic scoring and live transmission of results.
